questions.question: When traveling long distances, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take rest breaks.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long trips, take a break every 100 miles or two hours. Driving through the night or when you normally sleep increases the risk of fatigue.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Are helpful to remove water and oil from the air tanks.
Are used to move air to the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are helpful to remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems contains water and oil. These can damage the system if they build up. Air tank drain valves remove water and oil from the compressed air.

questions.question: Black ice is:

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road.
A thin layer of ice on the road.
Ice that is black from debris on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. It looks like a wet road. Watch for black ice when the road looks wet but the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: ____ is an example of required emergency equipment.
questions.correctAnswerText: A spare electrical fuse
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have required emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or three flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What is a retarder?

options.text: A device that prevents a vehicle from going too fast
A device that prevents a vehicle from being too loud
A device that improves a vehicle's gas mileage

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that prevents a vehicle from going too fast
questions.explanation: A retarder is a device that slows down a vehicle. It reduces how much drivers need to use the brakes.

questions.question: If one-fourth of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing when a vehicle is inspected:

options.text: The vehicle's driver will be allowed to drive, but only at reduced speeds.
The vehicle will be put out-of-service until it is fixed.
The vehicle will be fine to drive since most of the spring is in place.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle will be put out-of-service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: During vehicle inspection, check for broken or missing leaves in leaf springs. This is a serious safety issue. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle must be taken out of service.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle unattended:

options.text: The parking brake should be used.
The parking brake only needs to be used if the vehicle is parked on a slope.
The parking brake should not be used, as it can damage the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The parking brake should be used.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. However, do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if they are wet and the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: To prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when beginning to move, you can:

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before taking your foot off the brake pedal.
Place the vehicle in second gear.
Use the parking brake when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before taking your foot off the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To prevent your vehicle from rolling backward after a stop, partly engage the clutch before you take your foot off the brake pedal.

questions.question: If a vehicle is power steering-equipped, the hoses should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Checked for leaks.
questions.explanation: When checking a power steering system, inspect the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Pay close attention to checking the hoses for leaks.

questions.question: If driving so slowly that you could impede other drivers, you should:

options.text: Drive while using your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive while using your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic flow, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you. Check that local laws allow this.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, does stopping distance get longer or shorter?
questions.correctAnswerText: It gets longer.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, your tires have less grip. This means your vehicle needs more distance to stop.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection with two turn lanes, which lane should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: The right turn lane.
questions.explanation: Start your left turn from the right turn lane. You may need to swing right first to turn left safely. Always use the rightmost lane when two left turn lanes are available.

questions.question: When spring brakes are on, what should you never do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Push down the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Never push the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. The springs and air pressure together could damage your brakes.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Leave more space between you and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave more space between you and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Increase your distance from the car ahead. This reduces the need for sudden stops and gives the tailgater room to pass. Speeding up is not safe—the tailgater will likely follow just as closely at the higher speed.

questions.question: If your coolant temperature gauge goes above the highest safe temperature, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and check what's wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check what's wrong.
questions.explanation: Stop driving as soon as possible and find out what is wrong. High coolant temperature can cause engine failure or fire.

questions.question: When speeding up on a wet road or other slippery surface, how should you accelerate?

options.text: Don't worry about the road condition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Accelerate very slowly on slippery surfaces. This gives your tires the best chance to grip the road.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop, your vehicle should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not roll backward.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must not roll backward when you start moving. Rolling backward could hit the vehicle behind you.

questions.question: Does having ABS on only one axle help with braking control?

options.text: Yes, it gives you more control when braking.
It slows you down but won't fully stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it gives you more control when braking.
questions.explanation: ABS on any axle gives you better control when braking than having no ABS. Brake normally even if ABS is on only the tractor, trailer, or one axle.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, which trailer should be closest to the cab?
questions.correctAnswerText: The heaviest one.
questions.explanation: Put the heaviest loaded trailer closest to the tractor. The lightest trailer should go in the back.

questions.question: When is drowsy driving most common?
questions.correctAnswerText: At night.
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving happens most at night because your body naturally wants to sleep during these hours. Be extra careful if you must drive at night.
